study type: Proof-of-concept study with retrospective cohort analysis
cohort: The study included 26,077 births at the Royal Victoria Hospital in Montreal, Canada, between 2001 and 2009.
finding: Latent profile analysis classified 1.3% of births as growth-restricted, and these infants showed significantly higher risks of adverse outcomes, including those not identified by the conventional SGA proxy.
mod_finding: Growth-restricted infants classified by the model were significantly more likely to require an emergency cesarean delivery (42% vs. 15%).
birth_weight: All births were included; birthweight was a key variable in the classification model and SGA definition (birthweight < 10th percentile).
gest_age: All births were included; gestational age was implicitly considered as 'small for gestational age' (SGA) is a common proxy for fetal growth restriction.
